title: Product Launch Strategy
description: Your product team is preparing to launch a new fitness wearable into a crowded market where the first few months could define the product's reputation. Three launch strategies are on the table, each with a different path to customers, growth, and risk. Review the evidence and decide which strategy the company should pursue.
p1_persona: You are a product marketing lead responsible for positioning, early customer enthusiasm, and brand credibility. You are looking for a launch plan that creates demand without overpromising what the product can sustain.
p2_persona: You are a commercial strategy lead responsible for channels, unit economics, and scaling risk. You are looking for a launch plan that can grow efficiently while protecting the company from expensive missteps.
correct_rationale: Pooled, Community-First has 6 distinct positive signals (beta retention, organic social reach, waitlist conversion, firmware-iteration risk reduction, repeat purchase, lower CAC). Premium has 3 (P1-only); Mass Market has 3 (P2-only). P1 alone leans Premium; P2 alone leans Mass Market; pooled C dominates.
shared_info: The Premium Launch prices the wearable at $349 targeting fitness enthusiasts
The Mass Market Launch prices at $149 targeting casual users with broad retail distribution
The Community-First Launch prices at $199, starts with online community, then expands to retail
p1_unique_info: The Premium segment generated 45% gross margin in our last hardware launch — the highest of any segment
Premium positioning would let us partner with the leading fitness influencer in our target market, who has signalled interest at the $349 price point
Premium customers historically drive 4x the brand-advocacy referrals of mass-market customers in our category
The Community-First approach was tested with 500 beta users who showed 94% 90-day retention — the highest the company has ever recorded
Community-First beta users organically created 2,300 social media posts about the product without being asked
Community-First customers have a 38% repeat-purchase rate within 12 months in our category benchmarks
p2_unique_info: Mass Market unit economics improve sharply at scale — projected 28% margin at 500K units, vs single-digit margin at 50K units
Mass Market positioning has secured a tentative endcap deal with the largest national fitness retailer, contingent on a Q2 launch
Our category's growth is driven by casual users entering the market — this segment grew 31% YoY vs 6% for fitness enthusiasts
Pre-launch waitlist data shows Community-First positioning converted 3x more signups per ad dollar than Premium or Mass Market messaging
Community-First lets us iterate firmware based on engaged user feedback before scaling — reducing the risk of a public recall (recalls cost ~$2M each in our category)
Customer acquisition cost is projected at $14/user for Community-First vs $58/user for Premium and $32/user for Mass Market
anchor_rationale: The Premium Launch maximises per-unit revenue and brand positioning
